title: The Moon's Changing Face
objective: After this level you can explain Moon phases and why we only ever see one side of the Moon.
summary: Phases show how much of the Moon's sunlit half faces us, over a ~29.5-day cycle. The Moon is tidally locked, so the same side always faces Earth.

cards.headline: The Moon doesn't change shape. You're just seeing it from a different angle.
Half lit, always
cards.body: The Sun always lights up half of the Moon. As the Moon orbits Earth, we see different amounts of that lit half: a thin crescent, a half, the full face, then back again. Nothing is covering the Moon; only our viewing angle changes.
cards.callout: A full cycle takes about 29.5 days

cards.fact: We always see the same side of the Moon.
cards.context: The Moon, about 384,400 km away, is tidally locked: it turns exactly once per orbit. The far side isn't permanently dark. It gets as much sunlight as the near side; we just never see it from Earth. Its day and its month last the same time.

questions.explanation: The Sun always lights half the Moon; as it orbits, we see more or less of that lit half.

questions.prompt: Why do we always see the same side of the Moon?

options.label: It rotates once for every orbit around Earth
It doesn’t rotate at all as it orbits Earth
options.rationale: It does rotate: exactly once per orbit.

options.label: Its far side is always turned toward the Sun
options.rationale: Both sides get sunlight as the Moon orbits.

options.label: Earth’s shadow always hides the far side
options.rationale: Earth’s shadow only reaches the Moon during a lunar eclipse.

questions.explanation: The Moon is tidally locked: one rotation per orbit keeps the same face toward Earth.

questions.prompt: The Moon’s phases repeat about every 29.5 days. From Level 5: what drives Earth’s yearly cycle of seasons?

options.label: Earth’s changing distance from the Sun
options.rationale: Earth is closest to the Sun in January, during northern winter.

options.label: The Moon’s phases pulling on Earth’s weather
options.rationale: The Moon’s phases don’t cause the seasons.

options.label: Earth’s tilted axis as it orbits the Sun
The Sun’s brightness rising and falling each year
options.rationale: The Sun’s output barely changes over a year.

questions.explanation: The Moon’s phases come from its orbit around Earth. The seasons come from Earth’s ~23.5° tilt as it orbits the Sun.
